title: Hired from a cab: forming a five-piece band
summary: A man in a hackney cab, shouting 'musician', wanted an orchestra; Briggs took him to the Flea Pits and formed a five-piece with Salnave, a drummer, a pianist and a guitarist.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So, I said, 'Okay,' and I went to work with him, and I stayed with him, and one of the days, just a few days after, while I was going to one of his rehearsals 'cause he made arrangements, you know.
You saw the program?
Yes.
He was a reading musician. And he had certain arrangements. And we had a band rehearsal, and he was very precise and everything, you see. We had a band rehearsal, and I was walking
Briggs
down Rue Pigalle, Rue Fontaine, to go to his rehearsal with my instrument case in my hand, and I heard somebody yell, 'Monsieur, Monsieur, Musician, Musician.'
It was the only word I understood in French, 'cause it sounds almost the same.
And I -- so when I looked I saw a man, two persons in a hackney cab, you know, hackney, a horse and buggy.
Right.
And a man jumped out, and stopped me and started to speak in French, and I couldn't understand a word he was saying.-- just one or two words, you see.

All I could hear was 'Musician, Musician.' And not far from where we were, was another colored boy, a French boy, and he understood the word 'Musician,' and he saw an instrument, and he saw he has a good chance on me, you know.
And he came up and asked the man what he wanted. So the man told him that he
Briggs 145
was looking for an orchestra, 'cause he was a musician, you know, so this guy tried to muscle-in and take the job for himself. (Laughter). He tried to muscle-in and take the job for himself.

And a lady was passing, she heard me say, she heard what this guy was telling the boss, and she said, she spoke a little English, so she says to me, "You speak English?" I said, "Yes, yes." She said, "He's no good. He's trying to take your job from you. This man wants you."
So, I said, "Is that the case." I said, "Look," I said, "Ma'am, just tell the man he can get in the cab as well. Tell the man to drive us to this address, the Flea Pits."
I said, "They're plenty of my friends there who can explain to the man what he wants." And he did, but this colored boy, he didn't hesitate, he came, he came.
And some of the boys they spoke French, enough French to know, They told me
Briggs 146
what the man wanted, and everything. So this boy, he said, to them, "Me, I'm drummer, I play drums."

I said, "You play drums, maybe I'll take you, why not." So, I took him with me, and he played fairly well, and we got along, and I contacted Salnave, the same Salnave, the saxophone player back in France.
And I found a piano player, the only name I knew, we called him "Kid," that's the only name, I remember. He had never given us his name. Kid, that's all.

And we got a guitar player by -- guitar player, he was an ex-GI from World War I, Albert Smith, from New York, and just five of us. He went back to Belgium, I didn't want to go back to Belgium, but it was just one of those things. That's the business.
